Proposition
[Classification of two-dimensional singular strata] 1. 13.3.1\group surfaces Source: thurston:page-0326

The singular locus of a two-orbifold is a union of mirror arcs and circles, with isolated corner reflectors at endpoints of mirror arcs. Away from mirrors, isolated singular points have cyclic rotation groups.
Proof

\sketch Finite subgroups of the Euclidean isometry group fixing a point are cyclic rotations or include reflections. The fixed sets of reflections are lines, and intersections of reflection lines give corner points.

□
